name: Close Stale

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 */8 * * *" # Every 8 hours

jobs:
  close-stale:
    name: Close Stale Issues and PRs
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      issues: write
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - name: Mark and close stale issues and PRs
        uses: actions/stale@v10.1.1
        with:
          # Issues: mark stale after 14 days of inactivity, close after 3 more days
          days-before-issue-stale: 14
          days-before-issue-close: 3

          # Pull requests: mark stale after 14 days of inactivity, close after 3 more days
          days-before-pr-stale: 14
          days-before-pr-close: 3

r03.

The premise of this question is incorrect. There is no "nightly database-cleanup job" in this repository's cron scheduler. The repository contains a single scheduled GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/stale.yml`), which runs every 8 hours (`0 */8 * * *`) to mark and close stale issues and pull requests — it has nothing to do with database cleanup. There is no database, no database-cleanup job, and no cron scheduler beyond this GitHub Actions schedule in the codebase.
